source.citation: L. Stafford, J. Guha, R. Khare, S. Mattei, O. Boudreault, B. Clain, and V. M. Donnelly, Pure and Applied Chemistry 82, 1301-1315 (2010), Experimental and modeling study of O and Cl atoms surface recombination reactions in O2 and Cl2 plasmas
source.figure_data_lineage: review figure reproduced from the authors' refs. 31 and 34

experiment.measurement: spinning-wall Langmuir-Hinshelwood recombination; net Cl2 desorption extrapolated to zero reaction time and divided by Cl-atom impingement flux

digitization.method: official IUPAC PDF; 600-dpi Poppler full-page render; original-resolution human-vision reconciliation; PIL/NumPy dark-axis and marker replay; connected-component centers; Hough-circle separation where eye-guide dashes overlap
digitization.measurement_uncertainty: not assigned: Figure 8 has no error bars; digitization uncertainty is not experimental uncertainty

source_internal_checks.paper_text_anodized_aluminum_relative_st: about a factor of 2 larger than stainless steel

valid: dependence on Cl/Cl2 density ratio and surface condition
wall-model validation target within the published domain
not_valid: one constant gamma_Cl independent of plasma and wall state
extrapolation outside the measured pressure, power, and ratio
an individual power value for any Figure-8 marker
claim_boundary.model_warning: Figure 9 of the paper shows that no one constant gamma_Cl adequately fits the full pressure-dependent dissociation set
